study type: Retrospective registry analysis (non-randomized observational cohort study)
exposure: Bromocriptine treatment (in addition to standard heart failure treatment)
outcome: Composite endpoint of maternal outcome (death or hospital readmission within 6 months, or persistent severe left ventricular dysfunction at 6-month follow-up)
cohort: The participants were 552 peripartum cardiomyopathy (PPCM) patients from the EORP PPCM registry with available follow-up data.
finding: Bromocriptine treatment, in addition to standard of care, was associated with better maternal outcomes in women with peripartum cardiomyopathy after 6 months.
